summary.description: One sentence: what happens in the video.

premise.description: One sentence naming the relatable SITUATION the video is built on, not what appears on screen. Write it as a person would describe it to a friend. Examples: 'he takes hours to reply and she reads into it', 'they disagree about how much time to spend with his friends'. null if the video is not about a human situation.

hook.description: Verbatim spoken line and/or on-screen text in the first 3 seconds.

punchline.description: Verbatim final spoken or on-screen line, if the video lands on a turn, joke, or reversal. null otherwise.

transcript.description: Verbatim spoken words in order. null if no speech.

dialogue.description: The exchange, in order, when two or more people speak. Up to 12 turns; if longer, take the 12 that carry the exchange. Empty array if there is no back-and-forth.

speaker.description: Role label for who is speaking, 1-2 lowercase words. Examples: 'girlfriend', 'boyfriend', 'narrator', 'friend', 'therapist'.

line.description: Verbatim. Do not summarize, correct, or translate.

on_screen_text.description: Every distinct text overlay, verbatim, in order.

format.description: 2-4 words, lowercase noun phrase, for how the video is constructed - not what it is about. Examples: 'voiceover product demo', 'green screen reaction', 'two person skit', 'pov direct address', 'silent before after'.

format_traits.description: 0-3 further 1-3 word lowercase traits. Examples: 'fast cuts', 'trending audio', 'text only', 'pov framing', 'asmr', 'split screen', 'subtitled', 'single take'.

setting.description: 2-4 words, lowercase noun phrase. Examples: 'kitchen counter', 'car passenger seat', 'bedroom bed', 'dog park'.

topics.description: 2-5 subjects of the video, each a 2-4 word lowercase noun phrase. For relationship content name the SITUATION, not the genre: 'delayed text replies', 'meeting his friends', 'splitting rent' - never 'relationship advice' or 'couple content'.

topic_summary.description: One to two sentences of prose stating exactly what is being discussed or worked through in the video - the specific substance behind the short phrases in `topics`. Write it the way you'd explain the video's actual subject to someone who only saw the noun phrases. null if the video has no real subject beyond what `format`/`setting` already capture (e.g. pure ASMR, a silent product shot).

estimated_duration_sec.description: Approximate length of the video in seconds.

stage.description: Stage of the relationship depicted or discussed. Use 'not_applicable' when the video is not about a relationship.

conflict.description: The friction the video turns on. 'no_conflict' for purely affectionate or cute content. Use 'not_applicable' when the video is not about a relationship.

register.description: Emotional tone of the piece. Use 'not_applicable' when the video is not about a relationship. See `register_detail` for what this register is actually about.

resolution.description: How the video ends. Use 'not_applicable' when the video is not about a relationship. This is a single dominant label for clustering - see the standalone `advice` and `reassurance` objects to capture BOTH when a video does both, `resolution_detail` for what a punchline/escalation/unresolved ending is actually about, and `resolution_valence` for how it emotionally lands.

perspective.description: Whose side the video is told from. Use 'not_applicable' when the video is not about a relationship.

register_detail.description: The specific substance behind whichever `relationship.register` applies - what's being vented about, what the petty behavior is, what's bittersweet, cringe, funny, or affectionate about. All null when register is 'not_applicable' or 'advice' (advice's content lives in the standalone `advice` object).

content.description: One sentence: the specific thing driving the register. Examples for venting: 'he hasn't apologized after three days'. For petty: 'she rearranged his stuff after he left wet towels out'. null if register is not_applicable or advice.

topic.description: 2-4 words, lowercase noun phrase version of `content`. null if register is not_applicable or advice.

target.description: Role label of who or what the register is directed at (matching `dialogue[].speaker` where possible) - e.g. who is being vented about, who the pettiness targets. null if not directed at anyone specific, or register is not_applicable or advice.

resolution_detail.description: The substance behind `relationship.resolution` for values not already covered by the standalone `advice`/`reassurance` objects - what the punchline joke was actually about, what triggered an escalation, or what was left unresolved. All null when resolution is 'not_applicable', 'reassurance', or 'advice_given'.

content.description: One sentence: what the punchline joke, escalation, or unresolved tension is actually about. null unless resolution is punchline, escalation, or unresolved.

topic.description: 2-4 words, lowercase noun phrase version of `content`. null unless resolution is punchline, escalation, or unresolved.

mechanism.description: For resolution=punchline only: the rhetorical move the joke makes. 'not_applicable' for every other resolution value.

resolution_valence.description: How the ending emotionally lands for the viewer, independent of the mechanical `relationship.resolution` label - e.g. an 'unresolved' ending can be warm or tense, an 'escalation' can be comedic or genuinely tense. 'not_applicable' when the video is not about a relationship.

advice.description: Whether the video contains someone giving advice, and what the advice actually is - independent of `relationship.resolution`, so a video can register both `advice` and `reassurance` as present at once.

present.description: true if anyone (narrator, character, on-screen text) tells someone what they should do or think.

content.description: The advice itself - verbatim if spoken or on-screen, otherwise a close one-sentence paraphrase. null if present is false.

topic.description: 2-4 words, lowercase noun phrase, what the advice is about. Examples: 'responding to slow texters', 'setting a budget', 'confronting a friend'. null if present is false.

source.description: Who delivers the advice. 'not_applicable' if present is false.

specificity.description: 'general_platitude' for broad truisms ('communication is key'), 'specific_actionable' for a concrete step. 'not_applicable' if present is false.

reassurance.description: Whether the video contains someone reassuring or comforting another person, and what that reassurance actually is - independent of `relationship.resolution`, so a video can register both `advice` and `reassurance` as present at once.

present.description: true if someone is comforted, affirmed, or reassured, verbally or through action.

content.description: The reassurance itself - verbatim line if spoken, or a one-sentence description of the reassuring action ('pulls her into a hug'). null if present is false.

tone.description: How the reassurance is delivered. 'not_applicable' if present is false.

giver.description: Role label of who gives the reassurance, matching `dialogue[].speaker` where possible. null if present is false.

receiver.description: Role label of who receives it. null if present is false.

count.description: Distinct people appearing or voiced. 0 if none.

pairing.description: 'one_person_two_roles' when one creator plays both sides of an exchange.

dynamic.description: 2-5 lowercase words for how the pair plays off each other. Examples: 'anxious partner calm partner', 'both playful teasing', 'one lectures one deflects'. null if fewer than two people.

synthetic.description: Whether the people on screen are real. Judge only from artifacts you can actually see or hear - never from subject matter or polish.

signals.description: The specific artifacts that led to the judgement, each 1-4 lowercase words. Examples: 'warping hands', 'unblinking eyes', 'lips out of sync', 'flat prosody', 'background morphs'. Empty array if none observed.

certainty.description: Confidence in `presenter` specifically. Use 'low' freely - synthetic video is often indistinguishable.

pacing.description: How the video moves. Judgments only - cut counts, fps and duration are measured from the file, not reported here.

energy_arc.description: Shape of intensity across the video.

humor_sincerity.description: Ordinal, not a percentage. 'balanced' means the video genuinely turns on both.

speaker_dominance.description: Who carries the exchange, by speaking time. 'first' is whoever speaks first in `dialogue`. not_applicable if fewer than two speakers.

density.description: Subjective information rate - words, text and cuts together, as a viewer experiences it.

expression_beats.description: Up to 6 moments where a face visibly changes expression. Empty if no face is visible. Do not invent beats to fill the array.

products.description: Physical products shown or named. Empty if none.

name.description: 2-4 words, lowercase noun phrase for the object itself, no brand. Examples: 'ceramic slow feeder bowl', 'silicone lick mat'.

brand.description: Only if legible on screen or spoken aloud. Never inferred.

people.description: Named people mentioned or shown, verbatim. Not the creator unless named.

brands.description: Brands named aloud or legible on screen, verbatim.

places.description: Cities, countries, regions, or venues named or clearly shown by signage, verbatim.

organizations.description: Companies, clinics, shelters, retailers named, verbatim.

spoken_language.description: BCP-47 code of the speech, e.g. 'en', 'es'. null if no speech.

cta.description: 'tag_someone' covers 'tag your person', 'send this to him'.
